To upgrade: - Add the [client SDKs](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/start/hello-client) to your app or site. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/upgrade/#braintreejs

## Overview
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/>

- [snippet] Hierarchy: result = gateway.customer.create({ — `result = gateway.customer.create({` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#hierarchy
- [snippet] All errors on all levels: result.errors.each do |error| — `result.errors.each do |error| ` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#all-errors-on-all-levels
- [snippet] Errors at specific levels: result.errors.for(:customer).each do |error| — `result.errors.for(:customer).each do |error| ` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#errors-at-specific-levels
- [snippet] Errors at specific levels: result.errors.for(:customer).size — `# number of errors on customer` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#errors-at-specific-levels
- [snippet] Errors on specific attribute: result.errors.for(:customer).on(:email) — `result.errors.for(:customer).on(:email)` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#errors-on-specific-attribute
- [snippet] Base errors: result = gateway.subscription.update( — `result = gateway.subscription.update(` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#base-errors
- [snippet] Errors on add-ons/discounts: result = gateway.subscription.create({ — `result = gateway.subscription.create({` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#errors-on-add-onsdiscounts
- [definition] Overview — [error result objects](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/result-objects/ruby#error-results)when we can't process the API call because parameters are invalid. Validation errors contain the following: — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#overview
- [definition] Hierarchy — Errors are returned in a hierarchy that matches the parameter hierarchy. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#hierarchy
- [definition] All errors on all levels — To get the errors on _all levels_, call each on `result.errors`. You can also check `result.errors.size` for the number of total errors. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#all-errors-on-all-levels
- [definition] Errors at specific levels — To get errors at a _specific level_, use the `for` method. The `attribute` will indicate which attribute is invalid. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#errors-at-specific-levels
- [definition] Errors on specific attribute — You can also get errors at a specific level on a *specific attribute*. This is useful if you want to display error messages inline in your forms. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#errors-on-specific-attribute
- [definition] Base errors — Sometimes validation errors aren't caused by a specific input parameter. For example, canceled subscriptions can't be updated. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#base-errors
- [definition] Errors on add-ons/discounts — It is possible to add, update and remove many add-ons and discounts at once. If any of the add-ons or discounts contain errors, these errors will be indexed based on the order of the add-on or discount in the request (beginning at 0). — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/validation-errors/overview/#errors-on-add-onsdiscounts

## Overview
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/webhooks/overview/>

- [definition] Overview — For information on how to create or parse webhooks, go to — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/webhooks/overview/#overview
- [definition] Notification kinds — The notification kind, returned by calling kind on the notification object, reveals what triggered the webhook. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/webhooks/overview/#notification-kinds
- [definition] Attributes — All webhook notifications have a kind, a timestamp, and an additional attribute that is specific to the notification [type](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/webhooks/overview/#notification-kinds). — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/webhooks/overview/#attributes
- [definition] Triggers — The specific trigger conditions depend on the notification [kinds](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/webhooks/overview/#notification-kinds). — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/webhooks/overview/#triggers
- [definition] Exceptions — An is raised if the webhook notification you attempt to parse has an invalid signature. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/webhooks/overview/#exceptions

- [parameter] Production: URL=api.braintreegateway.com; Date Implemented=September 2025; Certificates=[Click here to download certificate files](https://paypalobjects.com/ppdevdocs/api.braintreegateway.com.zip) — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#ssl-certificates
- [definition] Best Practices — The SSL certificates for Braintree Mobile (iOS and Android) SDKs are set to expire on March 30, 2026. This will impact published versions of your app if they utilize older versions of the SDK. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#best-practices
- [definition] Autocomplete — When building a web form that has an input for a credit card number, turn off autocomplete so that your customer's browser won't save their credit card number. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#autocomplete
- [definition] Code vs text — Most responses from Braintree will include both a code and text. The text is the human-readable description and the code is meant to be consumed programmatically. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#code-vs-text
- [definition] Internet Explorer Quirks Mode — By writing invalid HTML syntax, you can cause versions of IE to enter Quirks Mode - a parsing mode that is designed to help render very old and/or invalid pages. Quirks Mode is unreliable and not supported by the JavaScript SDK, so the Drop-in UI may not appear in such cases. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#internet-explorer-quirks-mode
- [definition] Minimum required server SDK versions — It goes without saying, but we'll say it anyway: we always recommend using the latest versions of our SDKs. While older versions may still be supported, in order to communicate securely with the Braintree gateway, you must use at least the version indicated below. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#minimum-required-server-sdk-versions
- [definition] Timeouts — When using the server SDKs, keep in mind that some requests (like creating transactions) can take longer than expected since they rely on communicating with a payment processor. The Braintree gateway has a timeout of 60 seconds to accommodate for this. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#timeouts
- [definition] Token and ID lengths and formats — In order to avoid interruptions in processing, it's best to make minimal assumptions about what our gateway-generated tokens and identifiers will look like in the future. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#token-and-id-lengths-and-formats
- [definition] Transport Layer Security — Following the PCI Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) requirements, it's critical that you secure your connection to the Braintree gateway using Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 or higher, and serve any form that collects payment data in production over HTTPS. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#transport-layer-security
- [definition] TLS Cipher Suites — In addition to ensuring you use TLS 1.2 or higher when connecting to Braintree, your integration must support at least one of the following TLS cipher suites. You must support at least one cipher suite for the version of TLS used by your integration. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#tls-cipher-suites
- [definition] Testing — While you can successfully test our and over HTTP in all supported desktop and mobile browsers, you must use HTTPS if you wish to test our PayPal button in mobile webviews. Ultimately, we strongly encourage you to test all your flows over HTTPS to create a more realistic test environment. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#testing
- [definition] SSL Certificates — We make periodic updates to our root SSL provider for API traffic to align with security standards. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/best-practices/ruby#ssl-certificates

- [definition] Static — A single tokenization key may be reused indefinitely across many client apps. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/authorization/tokenization-key/#static
- [definition] Reduced privilege — Tokenization keys authorize only a subset of PayPal Braintree's client API capabilities. The SDK should function as with a client token, with some limitations: - When using a tokenization key, clients may only tokenize payment information. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/authorization/tokenization-key/#reduced-privilege
- [definition] Obtaining a tokenization key — To obtain a tokenization key, follow these steps: 1. - [definition] Adding a tokenization key to your app — Because of their reduced authorization, tokenization keys are publishable, meaning safe to include in your app. They are not sensitive information and can be exposed in an insecure client. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/authorization/tokenization-key/#adding-a-tokenization-key-to-your-app
- [definition] Initializing the SDK — Tokenization keys can be used with any version of the Android and iOS SDKs and JavaScript SDK v2.17 or higher. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/authorization/tokenization-key/#initializing-the-sdk

- [definition] Fastlane User Profiles — Fastlane supports two primary user types, each with different experiences: - **Guest User (Non-Accelerated):** A user who interacts with Fastlane without a recognized profile. These users experience the standard flow without acceleration. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/fastlane/overview/#fastlane-user-profiles

- [definition] Overview — Use the server-side shipping callback to dynamically update shipping options, taxes, and order totals when a consumer changes their shipping address or selects a different shipping option during PayPal checkout. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/paypal/features/shipping_module/#overview
- [definition] How it works — The shipping callback creates a real-time communication loop between PayPal and your server while the consumer is in the PayPal paysheet. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/paypal/features/shipping_module/#how-it-works
- [definition] Prerequisites — 1. **Braintree JS SDK v3.137.0+** (v3.137.0+ recommended for latest stability) 2. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/paypal/features/shipping_module/#prerequisites
- [definition] Callback request — When the consumer changes their shipping address or selects a different shipping option, PayPal sends an HTTP POST to your `shippingCallbackUrl` with the following JSON body. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/paypal/features/shipping_module/#callback-request
- [definition] Callback response — Your server must respond with HTTP `200 OK` and a JSON body containing the updated order details and shipping options. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/paypal/features/shipping_module/#callback-response
- [definition] Error handling — If you cannot fulfill shipping for the given address or option, respond with HTTP `422` using PayPal's error format: a `name` of `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` and a `details` array whose `issue` is the error code. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/paypal/features/shipping_module/#error-handling
- [definition] Domain registration — You must register your callback domain in the Braintree Control Panel before PayPal will send callbacks to your endpoint. Register separately in both **sandbox** and **production**. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/paypal/features/shipping_module/#domain-registration
- [definition] Best practices — 1. **Handle the first callback with no shipping option.** Your server must handle the first callback where`shipping_option` is absent. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/paypal/features/shipping_module/#best-practices

- [parameter] Some failed transactions are re-presented: Re-presentment is not available. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#settlement
- [definition] Overview — SEPA Direct Debit is currently in limited release and is only available to pilot merchants. If you want to participate in the pilot, please — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#overview
- [definition] How it works — SEPA Direct Debit can be offered as a payment choice in your checkout flow. Customers choosing to pay with SEPA Direct Debit will be asked to provide an IBAN that PayPal will validate before redirecting them to a mandate page. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#how-it-works
- [definition] Checkout flow — 1. Customer is presented with your checkout page and selects SEPA as their payment method 2. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#checkout-flow
- [definition] Mandate management — The mandate acceptance flow is used to display mandates, obtain customer authorization, and store accepted authorizations. The Mandate Management API allows you to view or revoke authorized mandates that have been collected in the acceptance flow. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#mandate-management
- [definition] Settlement — SEPA Direct Debit transactions usually take 2-3 business days to settle. The time frame and details of the settlement process vary depending on if your account is configured to use Instant or Delayed Settlement: — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#settlement
- [definition] Disputes and returns — Your customer can dispute any transaction with their bank. Disputes raised within 8 weeks of the transactions will be automatically honored in alignment with SEPA guidelines. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#disputes-and-returns
- [definition] Eligibility — PayPal Direct Banking Platform's SEPA Direct Debit solution is supported for bank accounts in the following countries: — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#eligibility
- [definition] SEPA risks — SEPA Direct Debit scheme does not guarantee funds as your customer or their bank can initiate disputes. - Any disputes raised by your customer with their bank within 8 weeks of the transactions will be automatically honored in alignment with SEPA guidelines. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#sepa-risks
- [definition] Recurring transactions and Vault support — Vaulting payment methods and creating recurring transactions is supported with SEPA Direct Debit. See our [vaulting docs](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/vaulting)for full instructions. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/sepa-direct-debit/overview/#recurring-transactions-and-vault-support

## Payment Orchestration Overview
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/>

- [definition] Payment Orchestration Overview — PayPal's Payment Orchestration is a layer that lets merchants connect to multiple PSPs or acquirers and value-added services through a single integration, so they can route and manage transactions without building and maintaining many direct connections. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#payment-orchestration-overview
- [definition] Available connectors — The following connectors are available. You can enable each connector through your Braintree account, and they require no client-side code changes. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#available-connectors
- [definition] Adyen — Braintree's partnership with Adyen provides global acquiring reach through Adyen's enterprise infrastructure with full wallet and 3DS support. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#adyen
- [definition] dLocal — Braintree's partnership with dLocal enables merchants to process transactions through local acquiring across 23 markets in Latin America and Southeast Asia, including Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Indonesia, and Japan. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#dlocal
- [definition] EBANX — Braintree's partnership with EBANX covers 13 markets, with strong Latin America (LatAm) coverage and additional reach into Africa, including Nigeria, Egypt, and South Africa. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#ebanx
- [definition] Fat Zebra — Braintree's partnership with Fat Zebra enables direct acquiring in Australia and New Zealand with support for digital wallets and local payment rails. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#fat-zebra
- [definition] FlexFactor — FlexFactor is a false-decline recovery engine. If a transaction fails on PayPal Enterprise, FlexFactor's real-time decision engine evaluates it and can recover revenue by routing through an alternative acquiring path. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#flexfactor
- [definition] Flutterwave — Braintree's partnership with Flutterwave enables card-not-present acquiring across Africa and emerging markets, supporting 22 currencies. This integration uses a non-public card-direct API distinct from Flutterwave's public-facing products. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#flutterwave
- [definition] Stripe — Braintree's partnership with Stripe enables processing in the United States only. It provides access to Stripe's acquiring infrastructure with broad card brand coverage. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#stripe
- [definition] Next steps — To get started, work with your Braintree account manager (AM) or technical account manager (TAM) to identify which connectors are appropriate for your markets. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/overview/#next-steps

- [definition] SETTLING status — When you capture or refund a transaction through Adyen, the initial status is `SETTLING`. Adyen processes these operations asynchronously and notifies Braintree of the outcome through a webhook. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/adyen/#settling-status
- [definition] FAILED status — A `FAILED` status occurs for system-level errors on authorization, void, and card verification when network issues or API errors prevent Braintree from receiving a valid response from Adyen. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/adyen/#failed-status
- [definition] Retries — Do not build a duplicate capture or refund retry loop when you see `success: true` with the `SETTLING` status. The transaction is pending while it waits for an asynchronous webhook from Adyen. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/adyen/#retries
- [definition] Network token support — Adyen supports network tokens. - [definition] Response codes — Braintree can only display a limited number of response codes, because Adyen controls transaction results. When Braintree cannot map Adyen decline codes to equivalent Braintree decline codes, Braintree returns code `2000` with the message `Do Not Honor`. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/adyen/#response-codes
- [definition] Processor response pass-through and debugging — Because Adyen controls approval and decline outcomes, Braintree surfaces a standardized set of result codes. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/adyen/#processor-response-pass-through-and-debugging
- [definition] CVV codes — Adyen CVV codes are the same as the CVV response codes that Braintree uses. Only authorization responses include the CVV response code. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/adyen/#cvv-codes

- [definition] Refusal response code mapping — Refusal response codes from Adyen are declines from the payment network after the transaction was processed. - [definition] FAILED status during charge — This is another rare event that could occur. Flutterwave's network focuses on Africa and emerging markets. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#flutterwave-integration-guide

- [definition] Before you begin — Integrating Flutterwave with Braintree requires configuration in both: - **In Braintree:** To process card transactions through Flutterwave, you need a Braintree merchant account that you configure for the Flutterwave connector. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#before-you-begin
- [definition] Transactions — The following topics describe the requirements for this integration. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#transactions

- [definition] Fields that Braintree passes to Flutterwave — The following tables list the fields Braintree passes to Flutterwave for each operation. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#fields-that-braintree-passes-to-flutterwave
- [definition] Customer creation — Creating a customer is optional for the Flutterwave integration. To create a customer, you can use either the Braintree SDKs or the GraphQL API. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#customer-creation
- [definition] Vaulted payment methods — Vaulting a tokenized payment method creates an entity that can be authorized or charged multiple times. A tokenized payment method also can be vaulted during authorization. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#vaulted-payment-methods
- [definition] CVV handling — For merchant-initiated transactions, such recurring transactions, or when using vaulted cards, Braintree does not send the CVV to Flutterwave. Instead, Braintree sends an empty string (`""`). — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#cvv-handling
- [definition] Supported transaction operations — The following table lists the transaction operations that the Flutterwave integration supports. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#supported-transaction-operations
- [definition] Transaction status mapping — The following table maps Flutterwave results to Braintree transaction statuses. For general information about Braintree result objects, see [result objects](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/result-objects/). — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#transaction-status-mapping
- [definition] SETTLING status and reconciliation — In rare cases, Flutterwave may return a retryable error (`SERVER_BUSY`, `SERVER_FAILED`, or an unrecognized error cause) after an otherwise-valid capture or refund request. When this occurs, the transaction is placed in `SETTLING` and Braintree automatically polls Flutterwave for the actual outcome. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#settling-status-and-reconciliation
- [definition] Charge operations — Charge for Flutterwave is dual-step. Braintree first performs an authorization and then immediately captures it. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#charge-operations
- [definition] Retries — Do not implement a retry loop when you observe `success: true` with a status of `SETTLING`. Braintree handles reconciliation automatically. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#retries
- [definition] Response codes — Flutterwave uses ISO 8583-style two-digit acquirer codes for declines. Braintree maps these to standardized Braintree response codes. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#response-codes
- [definition] CVV response code mapping — The following table maps Flutterwave CVV codes to their Braintree equivalents. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#cvv-response-code-mapping
- [definition] Failure response code mapping — The following table maps Flutterwave acquirer failure codes to their Braintree equivalents. If a Flutterwave acquirer code is not in this list, Braintree passes through the raw code and message in the `additionalProcessorResponse` field without a mapped `genericResponseCode`. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#failure-response-code-mapping
- [definition] Testing — Braintree provides a set of [test card numbers](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/testing#credit-card-numbers/) for sandbox testing. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#testing
- [definition] Expiration date-controlled outcomes — The expiration date you provide determines the outcome from Flutterwave for mapped test cards. Use the combinations that are in the following tables when you test your integration in the sandbox environment. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#expiration-date-controlled-outcomes
- [definition] Known limitations — Review the following known behaviors and limitations before processing transactions through Flutterwave. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#known-limitations
- [definition] Supported currencies — The Flutterwave connector supports the following currencies: GBP, CAD, XAF, CLP, COP, EGP, EUR, GHS, GNF, KES, MWK, MAD, NGN, RWF, SLL, STD, ZAR, TZS, UGX, USD, XOF, ZMW. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#supported-currencies
- [definition] Related content — The following resources provide additional information about the Flutterwave integration and Braintree platform: — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/orchestration/flutterwave/#related-content

## Best Practices and Security
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/>

- [parameter] Data isolation: Your data is isolated and accessible only to your authorized users — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#security
- [parameter] Data residency: Payment data remains in PayPal's Snowflake environment — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#security
- [parameter] Encryption at rest: AES-256 encryption for all stored data — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#security
- [parameter] Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ required for all connections — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#security
- [parameter] Access control: Managed via your Snowflake account's RBAC — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#security
- [parameter] Always use date filters: Reduces data scan volume — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#query-performance
- [parameter] Use `LIMIT` for exploration: Prevents large result sets — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#query-performance
- [parameter] Select specific columns: Reduces data transfer — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#query-performance
- [parameter] Use `fee_summary_v1`: Pre-aggregated for reports — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#query-performance
- [parameter] Filter by `TRANSFER_ID`: Leverages partition pruning — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#query-performance
- [definition] Best Practices and Security — This section covers security controls built into Data Lens and recommended practices for writing efficient queries. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#best-practices-and-security
- [definition] Security — Data Lens uses Snowflake Secure Data Sharing with row-level security. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#security
- [definition] Query performance — This table outlines best practices for writing efficient Data Lens queries. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/data-lens/best-practices/#query-performance

## Managing
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/disputes/managing/>

- [definition] Managing — Managing disputes via the API is only available to merchants who can access disputes in the Braintree Control Panel. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/disputes/managing/#managing
- [definition] Locate open disputes — When a cardholder's bank informs Braintree of a new dispute against a merchant account, a dispute object is created for that account with a status of `open`. From here, it is up to you to locate the dispute and decide how to respond to it. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/disputes/managing/#locate-open-disputes
- [definition] Using dispute webhooks — When you set up dispute webhooks, you will receive automated notifications of dispute-related events at a designated endpoint on your server. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/disputes/managing/#using-dispute-webhooks
- [definition] Using dispute search and find requests — If you prefer to actively check for open disputes, you can locate them using search and find API requests: - Use [`Dispute: Search`](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/dispute/search) to retrieve a collection of disputes based on criteria you specify - Use [`Dispute… — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/disputes/managing/#using-dispute-search-and-find-requests
- [definition] Respond to open disputes — When a cardholder initiates a dispute, it's assigned a [reason code](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/response/dispute#reason_code), which Braintree returns on the [dispute response object](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/response/dispute). — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/disputes/managing/#respond-to-open-disputes
- [definition] Accepting disputes — Sometimes, it is in your best interest to accept a dispute rather than fight it. You can do this using the [`Dispute: Accept`](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/dispute/accept) call. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/disputes/managing/#accepting-disputes
- [definition] Responding with evidence — If you do not wish to accept a dispute, you'll need to submit evidence showing why the dispute is not warranted. For most dispute reasons, you can submit whatever documentation you think will help your case. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/disputes/managing/#responding-with-evidence

## Overview
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/network-tokens/overview/>

- [definition] Intro — In times of economic uncertainty, merchants face unprecedented pressure to deliver results and grow their bottom line while ensuring a seamless and secure experience for their customers. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/network-tokens/overview/#intro
- [definition] What is Tokenization — Every credit or debit card is embossed with a string of numbers, typically around 16 digits—some are as short as 14 and as long as 19 depending on the card network and region—that identifies a cardholder and the corresponding issuing bank. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/network-tokens/overview/#what-is-tokenization
- [definition] What is Network Tokenization — Network Tokenization goes beyond tokenization and replaces a traditional primary account number (PAN) with a merchant-specific cryptographic token. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/network-tokens/overview/#what-is-network-tokenization

- [parameter] `approved`: A merchant has been approved for a Braintree account. All funds from settled transctions will be disbursed to the merchant's bank account. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-auth/webhooks/#connected-merchant-underwriting-status
- [parameter] `denied`: A merchant has been denied. All settled transactions will be refunded. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-auth/webhooks/#connected-merchant-underwriting-status
- [parameter] `application_submitted`: A merchant has submitted their application to Braintree. The merchant can now accept payments to a limit - 25 transactions or up to $2500. Funds will not be disbursed until the merchant is approved. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-auth/webhooks/#connected-merchant-underwriting-status
- [parameter] `under_review`: A merchant application is being reviewed. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-auth/webhooks/#connected-merchant-underwriting-status
- [parameter] `inactive`: A merchant decided to not move forward with the underwriting process. This also occurs if a trial merchant has not submitted an application within 30 days of processing their first payment. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-auth/webhooks/#connected-merchant-underwriting-status
- [parameter] `link`: A connected merchant has connected a PayPal account to their gateway and can accept PayPal payments. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-auth/webhooks/#paypal-account-status-changed
- [parameter] `unlink`: A connected merchant has disconnected the PayPal account from their gateway. They can no longer accept PayPal payments until they link another PayPal account to their gateway. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-auth/webhooks/#paypal-account-status-changed

## Card Verification
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/card-verification>

- [definition] Card Verification — Our card verification feature only works with credit and debit card payment methods. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/card-verification#card-verification
- [definition] How it works — The Braintree gateway verifies credit cards by running either a $0 or $1 authorization and then automatically voiding it. For most processors and card brands, transactions are initially tried with a $0 authorization. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/card-verification#how-it-works
- [definition] Enabling card verification — To enable card verification for all cards as they are entered into the Vault: 1. Log into the [Control Panel](https://www.braintreegateway.com/login) . — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/card-verification#enabling-card-verification
- [definition] Retrying all failed $0 verifications — Certain banks using Visa and Mastercard do not accept $0 as a valid transaction amount. These banks typically respond with a specific decline code that tells us that we should retry the authorization with an amount of $1, which we do automatically. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/card-verification#retrying-all-failed-0-verifications
- [definition] Verifying vaulted cards — Due to PCI compliance restrictions, we never store your customer’s CVV. You’ll need to collect this from them again before re-verifying a card through the Control Panel or API. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/card-verification#verifying-vaulted-cards

## Apple Pay
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay>

- [definition] Apple Pay — Apple Pay allows customers to make secure purchases using a credit or debit card associated with a supported Apple mobile device. Businesses can accept Apple Pay on newer versions of iOS and Safari, making it quick and easy for customers to buy on both mobile and the web. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#apple-pay
- [definition] Availability — Where your business is located dictates your ability to accept Apple Pay. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#availability
- [definition] Processing — Apple Pay transactions process and settle just like credit card transactions, but can be identified in the Control Panel by their unique payment type logo. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#processing
- [definition] Fees — There are no additional fees for processing Apple Pay transactions – pricing for Apple Pay is the same as your other credit card transactions. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#fees
- [definition] Disputes — Chargebacks, retrievals, and pre-arbitrations on Apple Pay transactions behave in the same way as your credit card disputes, and should be responded to according to your merchant account setup. If you’re unsure how to handle a dispute, — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#disputes
- [definition] Liability Shift — Apple Pay supports liability shift for all the major networks (Mastercard, Discover and Amex) with the following exceptions: - For Visa, liability shift is supported globally for devices running iOS 16.2 and above. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#liability-shift
- [definition] Fraud tools — Apple uses a tokenization system to encrypt card information and reduce the risk of fraud. As a result, our [Basic Fraud Tools](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/basic/overview) are not compatible with Apple Pay. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#fraud-tools
- [definition] Recurring billing and vaulting — Apple Pay cards can be vaulted and used for [recurring billing](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/recurring-billing/overview) and split shipment transactions. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#recurring-billing-and-vaulting
- [definition] Setup — Before getting started, you'll need to work with us and Apple to configure your Apple Pay certificates and Merchant IDs. Then you can complete your client (iOS and/or JavaScript v3) and server integrations. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#setup
- [definition] Certificate renewal — If you integrate with Apple Pay using our iOS client SDK, you will be required to configure an Apple Pay certificate before completing your integration. This certificate expires after 25 months and must be kept up-to-date to avoid any disruptions in your processing. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/apple-pay#certificate-renewal

## Google Pay
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/google-pay>

- [definition] Availability — Where your business is located dictates your ability to accept Google Pay. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/google-pay#availability

- [definition] Fees — There are no additional standard fees for processing Google Pay transactions. Pricing for Google Pay cards is the same as your other credit card transactions and is priced similarly to your other PayPal transactions. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/google-pay#fees
- [definition] Disputes — Chargebacks, retrievals, and pre-arbitrations on Google Pay transactions behave in the same way as your credit card or PayPal disputes, and should be responded to according to your merchant account setup. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/google-pay#disputes
- [definition] Fraud tools — We recommend collecting billing address information, at minimum billing postal code, and passing that billing postal code with all Google Pay transactions as a best practice. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/google-pay#fraud-tools
- [definition] Recurring billing and vaulting — Our support for vaulting Google Pay payment methods varies based on the payment method type: - Google Pay cards stored to a Google account can be vaulted for future transactions, [recurring billing](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/recurring-billing/overview) , and split… — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/google-pay#recurring-billing-and-vaulting
- [definition] Setup — To add Google Pay to your Braintree integration, you'll need to update your application code and make sure Google Pay is enabled in your Control Panel. Whether you're adding Google Pay to an Android app or integrating for web, you need to receive approval from Google before moving to production. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/google-pay#setup

## 3D Secure
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure>

- [definition] 3D Secure — 3D Secure (3DS) is an additional security layer for online credit and debit card transactions that adds an authentication step for customers making online purchases. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure#3d-secure
- [definition] Benefits — 3D Secure is safer than processing cards normally, for you and your customers. By enabling 3D Secure alongside Braintree's [fraud tools](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/overview), you can — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure#benefits
- [definition] Processing — With Braintree, a 3D Secure Lookup is performed during the checkout process. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure#processing
- [definition] Compatibility — 3D Secure is only compatible with credit card, debit card, and transactions. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure#compatibility
- [definition] Card brands — Most card brands have their own 3D Secure services. We support the following: - Visa Secure (formerly known as Verified by Visa) - MasterCard Identity Check and MasterCard SecureCode (including Maestro) - Discover ProtectBuy (including Diners Club) - American Express SafeKey — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure#card-brands
- [definition] Fees — Depending on your pricing model, there may be an additional per transaction fee to process 3D Secure transactions. If you’re unsure which pricing model you’re on, [Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help/feeHelp) for fee information. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure#fees
- [definition] Chargebacks — In certain cases, 3D Secure can shift liability for chargebacks due to fraud from you to the customer’s bank. Liability shifts for fraudulent chargebacks will be based on the transaction's status code. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure#chargebacks
- [definition] Setup — To start supporting 3D Secure, please read our [3D Secure developer docs](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/3d-secure/overview) and then [contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help/FraudProtectionQuestion) to enroll. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure#setup
- [definition] Confirm setup — You can confirm that your account has been set up for 3D Secure in the Control Panel. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/3d-secure#confirm-setup

## Gateway Rejections
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/transactions/gateway-rejections>

- [definition] Gateway Rejections — Gateway rejections are not the same as declines. Gateway rejections are blocked by your gateway settings, while declines are blocked by the customer's bank. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/transactions/gateway-rejections#gateway-rejections

## AVS and CVV Rules
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/basic/avs-cvv-rules>

- [definition] AVS and CVV Rules — AVS and CVV rules only apply to credit cards. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/basic/avs-cvv-rules#avs-and-cvv-rules
- [definition] How AVS and CVV rules work — When you submit a transaction or verification request for a new credit card, we pass the address and CVV information provided to the card-issuing bank. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/basic/avs-cvv-rules#how-avs-and-cvv-rules-work
- [definition] Enabling AVS and CVV rules — To enable AVS and CVV rules: 1. Log into the 2. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/basic/avs-cvv-rules#enabling-avs-and-cvv-rules
- [definition] Recommended setup options — It's best practice for most merchants to collect CVV information — this can help lower the risk of fraudulent transactions and can be used as supporting evidence in your favor if the customer issues a Regardless of whether you choose to verify the CVV, selecting to reject transactions if *CVV is… — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/basic/avs-cvv-rules#recommended-setup-options
- [definition] AVS and CVV rules in the Vault — By default, AVS and CVV rules only apply to first time transactions and will not be applied to recurring payments or any transactions created using credit cards stored in the Vault. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/basic/avs-cvv-rules#avs-and-cvv-rules-in-the-vault
- [definition] Maestro cards and CVV rules — If you have CVV rules enabled in the Control Panel, you must pass CVV information with every submitted credit card transaction or verification. Because Maestro cards do not typically include a CVV, you may find that your CVV rules reject most attempted Maestro transactions and verifications. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/basic/avs-cvv-rules#maestro-cards-and-cvv-rules
- [definition] Overriding rejections — When creating transactions via the API, you can selectively skip and checks. Alternatively, you can always ask the customer to provide a different payment method. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/basic/avs-cvv-rules#overriding-rejections

## Setup Guide
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide>

- [definition] Setup Guide — Once you have confirmed that your merchant account is [eligible to accept PayPal transactions](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/overview#availability), you must complete the following steps to add this payment method to your Braintree integration: — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide#setup-guide
- [definition] Sign up for a PayPal Business Account — In order to use PayPal with Braintree, you'll need a PayPal Business Account. You can either sign up for a new account on [PayPal's website](https://www.paypal.com/webapps/mpp/referral/paypal-business-account), or upgrade an existing by completing the following steps: — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide#sign-up-for-a-paypal-business-account
- [definition] Enter your PayPal credentials in the Braintree Control Panel — You must enter your PayPal Business Account credentials in the Braintree Control Panel to enable this payment method in production. You can only link one PayPal account to your Braintree gateway. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide#enter-your-paypal-credentials-in-the-braintree-control-panel
- [definition] Managing disputes in the Braintree Control Panel — To keep your transaction management in a centralized location, we recommend enabling PayPal disputes in your Braintree Control Panel. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide#managing-disputes-in-the-braintree-control-panel
- [definition] Settlement Withdrawal — To keep funding as simple as possible, we recommend that you enable Settlement Withdrawal on your account by [contacting PayPal](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide#contacting-paypal-support). — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide#settlement-withdrawal
- [definition] eCheck payments — An eCheck, or electronic check, is a payment sent directly from your customer's bank account. **Braintree does not support these transactions at this time**. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide#echeck-payments
- [definition] Foreign currencies — To accept PayPal payments in multiple currencies, you must first complete the following steps: - Confirm that you have a Braintree merchant account for each currency you'd like to accept – [contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help/acceptCurrencies) if you need assistance - Set up… — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide#foreign-currencies
- [definition] Contacting PayPal support — Many account changes can be made directly in your PayPal console (e.g. your funding bank account), but you may need to call to request certain setup options (e.g. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/paypal/setup-guide#contacting-paypal-support

## Getting Started
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview>

- [parameter] Net Settlement: D+1 (1 day after disbursement) — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview#when-you-receive-it
- [parameter] Gross Settlement: D+2 (2 days after disbursement) — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview#when-you-receive-it
- [parameter] `merchant_acct`: What it means=Your Merchant Account ID; Example=`acme_prod` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview#file-naming-convention
- [parameter] `YYYYMMDD`: What it means=Disbursement date (bank transfer date); Example=`20260115` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview#file-naming-convention
- [parameter] `1-1`: What it means=File sequence (file 1 of 1); Example=`1-3` means file 1 of 3 — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview#file-naming-convention
- [parameter] `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS`: What it means=Generation timestamp (UTC); Example=`20260117T143022` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview#file-naming-convention
- [parameter] "Which DFR row matches my bank statement?": `Transfer ID` in Report Summary — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview#key-fields-for-bank-reconciliation

- [parameter] **Positive (+)**: Money is flowing...=TO you; Examples=Sales, Chargeback Reversals, Reserve Releases — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview#sign-convention
- [parameter] **Negative (−)**: Money is flowing...=FROM you; Examples=Refunds, Chargebacks, Fees, Reserve Holds — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/overview#sign-convention

## Field Reference
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference>

- [parameter] `Merchant Account ID`: Data Type=String; Nullable=No; Description=The merchant account that processed these transactions — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#core-reconciliation-fields
- [parameter] `Transfer ID(s)`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Bank statement reference. **PRIMARY RECONCILIATION KEY.** Match exactly to the bank statement. If Net Disbursed exceeds banking limits, multiple Transfer IDs will be comma-separated. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#core-reconciliation-fields
- [parameter] `Bank Account`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Last 2 digits of the receiving bank account. Useful if multiple bank accounts configured. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#core-reconciliation-fields
- [parameter] `Currency`: Data Type=String (ISO 4217); Nullable=No; Description=ISO 4217 3-letter currency code. All monetary amounts in this row are in this currency. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#core-reconciliation-fields
- [parameter] `Net Disbursed Amount`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Actual bank deposit/withdrawal. **MUST MATCH THE BANK STATEMENT.** — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#core-reconciliation-fields
- [parameter] `Sales`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Sum of Gross Settlement Amount for all Sale records — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-breakdown-fields
- [parameter] `Refunds`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Sum of Gross Settlement Amount for all Refund records (includes Referenced and Non-Referenced) — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-breakdown-fields
- [parameter] `Disputes`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Net sum of chargebacks and chargeback reversals — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-breakdown-fields
- [parameter] `Returns`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Sum of all Returns (ACH/direct debit failures) — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-breakdown-fields
- [parameter] `Adjustments`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Sum of all Adjustments (reserve movements, manual adjustments) — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-breakdown-fields
- [parameter] `Other`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Sum of Gross Settlement Amount where Record Type is not Sale, Refund, or Dispute — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-breakdown-fields
- [parameter] `Gross Fees`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Total fees tracked but not yet debited. Gross Settlement only; zero in Net Settlement. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-breakdown-fields
- [parameter] `Net Fees`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Total fees already deducted from transactions. Net Settlement only; zero in Gross Settlement. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-breakdown-fields
- [parameter] `Balance`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Funds held in system balance due to bank issues. Contact support if populated. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#error-recovery-fields
- [parameter] `Previous failed disbursement amount(s)`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Amount from a prior failed transfer now included in this transfer. Multiple values comma-separated. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#error-recovery-fields
- [parameter] `Previous transfer ID(s)`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Transfer ID of the failed disbursement being recovered. Multiple values comma-separated. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#error-recovery-fields
- [parameter] `Record ID`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Unique identifier for this transaction or event. Primary key for tracking. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#identification-fields
- [parameter] `Merchant Account ID`: Data Type=String; Nullable=No; Description=The merchant account that processed this record. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#identification-fields
- [parameter] `Transfer ID`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Links this record to its RS summary row. Used to reconcile deposit entries against line items. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#identification-fields
- [parameter] `Order ID`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Your internal order/transaction reference (only present if passed at transaction time). Used to cross-reference with your internal systems. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#identification-fields
- [parameter] `Customer Id`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Unique identifier for the customer. Can be Braintree-generated or merchant-supplied at customer record creation. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#identification-fields
- [parameter] `Record Type`: Data Type=String; Nullable=No; Description=High-level category: Sale, Refund, Dispute, Return, Fees, Adjustments, Transfer, Failed Disbursement — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#transaction-classification-fields
- [parameter] `Record Subtype`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Specific classification within Record Type. New subtypes may be introduced with new fees and regional availability. See [Transaction Types](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/transaction-types) for all values. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#transaction-classification-fields
- [parameter] `Account Name`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Business name visible to the consumer. Primary value is the Descriptor set in the API; secondary value is Business name on file. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#account-fields
- [parameter] `Account ID`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Account ID for the specific Payment Instrument. For American Express Direct: the Amex Account ID. For Venmo (US only): Venmo Profile ID. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#account-fields
- [parameter] `Created At`: Data Type=DateTime; Nullable=No; Description=UTC timestamp when record was created. Format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#datetime-fields
- [parameter] `Settlement Date`: Data Type=Date; Nullable=Yes; Description=Date the card network confirmed settlement. Local timezone to acquiring region. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#datetime-fields
- [parameter] `Disbursement Date`: Data Type=Date; Nullable=Yes; Description=Date the bank transfer was initiated. Local timezone to acquiring region. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#datetime-fields
- [parameter] `Presentment Currency`: Data Type=String (ISO 4217); Nullable=Yes; Description=Currency of original customer transaction (e.g., USD, CAD, AUD) — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#currency-conversion-fields
- [parameter] `Gross Presentment Amount`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Transaction amount in customer's native currency — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#currency-conversion-fields
- [parameter] `Exchange Rate`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Conversion rate from Presentment to Settlement currency — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#currency-conversion-fields
- [parameter] `Settlement Currency`: Data Type=String (ISO 4217); Nullable=No; Description=Your configured settlement currency — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#currency-conversion-fields
- [parameter] `Gross Settlement Amount`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Transaction amount in settlement currency before fees (the "face value") — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-fields
- [parameter] `Total Gross Fees`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Fees accrued for later billing (Gross Settlement only) — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-fields
- [parameter] `Total Net Fees`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Fees deducted immediately (Net Settlement only) — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-fields
- [parameter] `Net Disbursed Amount`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Amount contributing to bank transfer. Calculated as: Gross Settlement Amount − Total Net Fees — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-fields
- [parameter] `Tax Amount`: Data Type=Decimal; Nullable=Yes; Description=Tax amount passed during transaction (presentment currency). Null if not provided. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-fields
- [parameter] `Tax Exempt`: Data Type=Boolean; Nullable=Yes; Description=Whether transaction was marked tax exempt. Merchant-supplied value. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#amount-fields
- [parameter] `Original Record ID`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Links to original sale for refunds/disputes. A refund record contains the Original Record ID of the Sale. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#linking-fields
- [parameter] `Original Order ID`: Data Type=String; Nullable=Yes; Description=Order ID of the original Sale transaction — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/disbursement-fee-report/field-reference#linking-fields

## Local Payment Methods
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods>

- [parameter] *Created*: Payment has been initiated by customer — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#statuses
- [parameter] *Expired*: Payment has been abandoned/cancelled by customer — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#statuses

- [parameter] *Transacted*: Merchant has attempted to complete the payment. At this point the Payment Context can show         up in the **Transaction Search** as*Settled* . — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#statuses
- [definition] Local Payment Methods — Local Payment Methods allow customers to pay with banks, wallets, or other means that operate only in specific regions of the world. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#local-payment-methods
- [definition] Availability — Local Payment Methods are available to eligible merchants in [all countries that Braintree supports](https://www.braintreepayments.com/country-selection). — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#availability
- [definition] Customer Availability — Different Local Payment Methods are available to customers depending on their locality. - [definition] Setup — The only setup required for Local Payment Methods is to ensure you have a valid PayPal business account in the Braintree Control Panel. You can then complete your client and server integrations. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#setup
- [definition] Fees — Braintree does not charge additional processing fees for Local Payment Methods; you are only subject to the pricing and fee rates established by PayPal as per your user agreement. If you are unsure of these rates, you will need to — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#fees
- [definition] Funding — Funds for Local Payment Methods will be settled into your PayPal account once your customer confirms a payment. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#funding
- [definition] Disputes — Disputes are currently not supported for Local Payment Methods. Customers will need to work directly with their bank to handle disputes. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#disputes
- [definition] Recurring transactions and vaulting support — Vaulting payment methods and creating recurring transactions are currently not supported with Local Payment Methods. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#recurring-transactions-and-vaulting-support
- [definition] Payment Contexts — Since most Local Payment Methods require you to redirect your customer to the Local Payment Method’s checkout flow, you can lose sight of customer activity as they are going through their checkout journey. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/local-payment-methods#payment-contexts
- [definition] Statuses — When a buyer clicks on a payment method, a Payment Context is created. ## Billing Cycles
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/recurring-billing/billing-cycles>

- [definition] Billing Cycles — Our recurring billing feature allows you to specify the length of a billing cycle, the billing date for a plan or subscription, and the number of billing cycles a subscription will last. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/recurring-billing/billing-cycles#billing-cycles
- [definition] How it works — When creating a plan, you'll be able to specify the following *Billing Details*: - billing cycle length - billing date - number of billing cycles — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/recurring-billing/billing-cycles#how-it-works
- [definition] Billing cycle length — The length of a billing cycle is the number of months between billing dates for a subscription plan. If a billing cycle is 3 months long, for example, then a customer on that subscription will only be charged 4 times a year, on the specified billing date. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/recurring-billing/billing-cycles#billing-cycle-length
- [definition] Billing date — You can choose to have the billing cycle of a new plan start immediately when the customer signs up, or on a future date. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/recurring-billing/billing-cycles#billing-date
- [definition] Number of billing cycles — You can set the length of a plan or subscription by selecting the number of billing cycles before expiration. For example, if a plan's billing cycle is 3 months long, and the number of billing cycles specified is 4, then the plan will expire after one year. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/recurring-billing/billing-cycles#number-of-billing-cycles

## Refund Authorizations
<https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations>

- [definition] Approved refunds — If a refund authorization is approved, the issuer has indicated, in real time, that they will accept the refund and deposit it into the cardholder’s account. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#approved-refunds
- [definition] Declined refunds — If the refund authorization is declined, the issuer has indicated, in real time, that the cardholder’s account is not capable of accepting the refund. A refund decline prevents the cardholder’s payment method from being refunded. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#declined-refunds
- [definition] Background — Refund authorizations are intended to help solve two industry challenges: — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#background
- [definition] Cardholder transparency for refunds — Refunds do not immediately appear on cardholder statements, which can cause cardholder confusion and frustration. This confusion can lead to increased refund-related customer support inquiries. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#cardholder-transparency-for-refunds
- [definition] Refund resolution timeliness — Issuers are not required to accept refunds. However, without an authorization framework, it can take days for you to be notified after an issuer rejects a refund. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#refund-resolution-timeliness
- [definition] Benefits — With the introduction of refund authorizations, cardholders can see the following benefits: — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#benefits
- [definition] Improved cardholder transparency — If a refund authorization is approved by the issuer, the issuer should immediately add a pending refund line item to the cardholder’s statement. This pending line item provides real time evidence to the cardholder that you’ve initiated the refund process. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#improved-cardholder-transparency
- [definition] Real time refund approval responses — If the cardholder’s account cannot accept the refund, the issuer will decline the refund authorization in real time. This real time response allows you to take immediate action if the refund is declined, such as requesting an alternate payment method in order to reattempt their refund. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#real-time-refund-approval-responses
- [definition] Reduction in refund-related disputes — By being more proactive, you can increase the timeliness of refund resolutions, which should reduce disputes from cardholders anxious for their refunds. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#reduction-in-refund-related-disputes
- [definition] How to handle refund declines — You should first attempt to refund the original sale transaction via Braintree’s [refund API](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/refund) or in the [Control… — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#how-to-handle-refund-declines
- [definition] Refund policies — It’s important to note that your refund/return policy still allows you to restrict or refuse refunds, returns, cancellations, or exchanges, provided that your policy outlines this clearly and was properly disclosed to your customer during the original sale transaction. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#refund-policies
- [definition] Current refund workflow — Braintree’s refund API assumes success for credit card, Apple Pay, and Google Pay-based refunds. This means that refund responses indicate the success of the API request itself, but not the overall outcome of the refund. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#current-refund-workflow
- [definition] Future refund workflow — Once the refund authorization framework is released by Braintree by card network and region, [refund requests](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/refund/all) will return real time [processor… — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#future-refund-workflow
- [definition] Technical changes — To reduce integration friction, Braintree will introduce two refund decline workflows. The workflow that you experience will depend on the SDK version your integration uses to connect to Braintree: new SDK versions or previous SDK versions. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#technical-changes
- [definition] Previous SDK versions — If your integration uses an SDK version older than those listed above, and the processor declines a refund, you will receive one of the following two in lieu of a processor response code: - **Hard decline: 915200** - Failed to refund transaction. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#previous-sdk-versions
- [definition] Sandbox testing — These changes are currently available in the [Braintree sandbox](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/testing). We recommend testing refund declines so that you can prepare for the upcoming launch of refund authorizations. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/refund-authorizations#sandbox-testing

- [definition] Success results — If the API call was successful, the `success?` on the result will return {true}. The target object will be available as a member of the result object. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/result-objects/ruby#success-results
- [definition] Error results — If the API call was not successful, the success on the result will return {false}. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/result-objects/ruby#error-results
- [definition] Message — The *message*on the error result gives a human-readable description of what went wrong, regardless of the cause and nature of the error. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/result-objects/ruby#message
- [definition] Params — Error results include the *parameters*that were submitted. This can be useful during Transparent Redirects to repopulate your form if validations fail. — https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/result-objects/ruby#params
